title: CRLR/89/2013 of Smt. Rashmi Agarwal AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
(1) Criminal Revision No.89 of 2013
Smt. Rashmi Aggarwal & another
 ÖÖÖ. Revisionists
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and another
..Ö. Respondents
Mr. SRS Gill, Advocate for the revisionists.
Mr. V.K. Jemini, Dy. Adv. Gen. (Cri.) for the State/respondent no.1.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar Aggarwal, Advocate for respondent no.2.
With
(2) Criminal Revision No.147 of 2013
Akhilesh Kumar
 ÖÖÖ. Revisionist
Vs.
Smt. Rashmi Aggarwal and another
..Ö. Respondents
Mr. Sudhir Kumar Agarwwl, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. SRS Gill, Advocate for the respondents.
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 As both the revisions, titled above, arise out of
the same judgment dated 2.4.2013 rendered by learned
Judge, Family Court, U.S. Nagar, hence are being
adjudicated together hereinbelow.
 By the impugned judgment, Smt. Rashmi
Aggarwal along with her one daughter Km. Niyati has
been awarded maintenance to the tune of Rs.2,000/-
each, in all Rs.4,000/-, to be payable by the husband
Akhilesh Kumar. Another daughter Km. Sheetal is
residing with the husband Akhilesh whereas the wife
along with her daughter is residing in the
accommodation owned by her husband.

2
 Learned counsel for the husband-Akhilesh has
vehemently contended that the impugned judgment
suffers with infirmity to the effect that without
determining his exact income, such maintenance has
been awarded. The finding of the Trial Court is based on
the assumption that the husband is employed at least in
some private shop, to earn a good income. All the same,
there is no concrete and credible evidence available on
record regarding his employment.
 Learned counsel has placed reliance on the
following two precedents: -
1. Bhagwan Dutt v. Smt. Kamla Devi and another,
[1975] 0 AIR (SC) 83/[1975] 0 SCC (Cri) 563
(Supreme Court).
2. Ram Singh v. State, [1963] 0 AIR (All) 355
(Allahabad High Court).
 The precedents, as relied by the learned
counsel, contemplate about the provisions of Section 488
of old Cr.P.C. which was almost analogous to the current
provision of Section 125 Cr.P.C. with a little difference.
In the old provision, the wife was entitled to claim
maintenance irrespective of her capability to maintain
herself. Now, under the current provision, the wife is
required to prove her incapacity or incapability to
maintain herself.
 In the instant case, the husband has made
averment that by knitting/stitching/embroidery work,
his wife earns Rs.10,000/- per month but the Trial Court
has opined that on this fact, no concrete and substantial
evidence has been produced by him. So, the Court can

3
discern that such a destitute wife, even if by doing some
work viz. stitching/embroidery/knitting etc., can hardly
be able to earn such a handsome amount, inasmuch as,
to the tune of Rs.10,000/- per month while the husband,
who, not an infirm person, is unable to earn even that
much. The Court finds that the relevant law, as has
been envisaged u/s 125 Cr.P.C. makes it mandatory
upon the husband to maintain his wife and child if he is
healthy and able-bodied, disregard of the fact whether he
is gainfullyA employed in some private or public sector
institution.
 At last, it was argued that the amount of
maintenance should be modified from the date of order
and not from the date of application. The Court does not
feel any substance in this argument too and thus, rejects
the same.
 The Court also finds that awarding of
Rs.4,000/-, in total, is not an excessive amount for such
a destitute wife along with her daughter to meet her both
ends meal, notwithstanding, she might have been
earning few hundreds of rupees by way of stitching etc.
 So, the revision filed by the husband (CRLR
No.147/2013) is bereft of any merit and is hereby
dismissed. Interim order dated 20.6.2013 is vacated.
 At the same time, Smt. Rashmi Aggarwal
though has filed revision (CRLR No.89/2013) challenging
the same judgment and her learned counsel has prayed
for the enhancement of the amount of maintenance but
the Court finds that there is no prayer made to that
effect in her revision. So, her revision is also dismissed.
It is, however, observed that the respondent-wife would

4
be at liberty to move an application under the relevant
provisions before the court below for enhancement of the
amount of maintenance.
 Let the LCR be returned to the court
concerned along with a copy of this order.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
 15.07.2014
Rdang
